stances_toward.note: France is Armenia's main European arms and political partner: first arms agreement in October 2023, a June 2024 contract for 36 Caesar howitzers, Bastion armoured vehicles, GM200 radars and Mistral missiles in the pipeline, a Defence Cooperation Programme for 2025, and French backing at the OSCE for the Minsk Group closure. Partner, not ally: no defence treaty. Bond - affinity: the French-Armenian community (Paris diaspora mobilisation conference, Apr 2026) and the shared view of Azerbaijan.

stances_toward.note: The sharpest quarrel with a Western state: France is Armenia's main Western arms supplier (announced Oct 2023, after which Aliyev withdrew from a meeting with Pashinyan), and Baku founded the Baku Initiative Group against 'French colonialism' (July 2023) which France accuses of amplifying the New Caledonia unrest in 2024 (Baku denies). Competition without a will to destroy, so rival. Warming in 2026: Aliyev-Macron call in May, Bayramov-Barrot meeting at the UNGA81 in September, and Aliyev's July message speaks of a new era.

stances_toward.note: Treaty of friendship and cooperation signed in Nancy in May 2025; on 2 Mar 2026 Macron offered a 'nuclear alliance' to eight European countries including Poland, Tusk confirmed talks, and on 20 Apr 2026 in Gdansk the two leaders spoke of information exchange, joint exercises and the possible presence of French nuclear-capable aircraft (Tusk: 'not my dream'). Warming because Paris is Warsaw's chosen second guarantor; the Weimar triangle gives it a format with Berlin. Bond - affinity.
